s1.syndrome_frame: Painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema on the face with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema below the left lower eyelid
Focal, non-tender, indurated elevation along the inferior orbital rim
Granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and extensive mucin
key_facts: 69-year-old woman
Several-month history of a painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema
History of chronic scleritis treated with NSAIDs
Left levator resection for ptosis
Dacryocystorhinostomy one month before the onset of the lesion
Mass persisted despite two courses of antibiotics
CT scan showed soft-tissue thickening of the anterior-inferior orbital rim and lower eyelid
No extension into surrounding structures or bony invasion
Excisional biopsy performed
Intraoperative frozen sections revealed granulomatous inflammation
Final histopathology showed granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and extensive mucin
No evidence of malignancy
Bacterial and fungal stains were negative

shortlist.label: Granuloma annulare
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology shows granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and extensive mucin, consistent with granuloma annulare

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Although not all defining features are present, the presence of granulomatous inflammation and mucin makes it a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation is a hallmark of sarcoidosis, and the periocular location is consistent with lupus pernio, a form of sarcoidosis

shortlist.label: Foreign body granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: The history of recent surgery and the presence of granulomatous inflammation raise the possibility of a foreign body reaction

shortlist.label: Periocular granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: The location of the lesion and the presence of granulomatous inflammation make this a plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The final histopathology showed granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and extensive mucin, which is consistent with granuloma annulare, and the clinical presentation of a painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema also supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The histology lacked the defining features of necrobiotic xanthogranuloma

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of systemic symptoms or other organ involvement typical of sarcoidosis

rejected.label: Foreign body granuloma
rejected.why: There is no history of trauma or foreign body exposure to suggest this diagnosis

rejected.label: Periocular granuloma
rejected.why: This is a more general term and granuloma annulare is a more specific diagnosis that fits the clinical and histological findings
